reason: Record the later owner instructions: fixed 1,536 dimensions supersede the ladder and smallest-passing decision; paid corpus construction before frozen development labels and a $10 editable shared cap are authorized. Preserve independently reviewed/frozen quality evaluation, all numerical acceptance thresholds, ledger-safe cutover and rollback requirements. This is a requirements correction, not a completion or activation claim.
goal: Run BidMate on PostgreSQL with pgvector-backed retrieval using validated 1,536-dimensional text-embedding-3-large corpus and query embeddings, preserving all application records, evidence identities, and billing guarantees through migration and cutover.
out: Unrelated frontend redesign, authentication, new data feeds, and answer-generation model changes.
Unrelated parsing, OCR, chunking, or answer-quality repairs from the earlier direct-RAG specification; preserve their behavior and outstanding findings.
Replacing Kiwi BM25 with PostgreSQL full-text ranking.
Enabling multiple application workers merely because PostgreSQL supports concurrent connections.
Mandatory HNSW adoption or an assumed improvement in retrieval accuracy or speed.
done: git diff --check

Inspect current main, workspace edits, effective configuration, database schema, runtime artifacts, embedding caches, and every SQLite/NumPy persistence caller. Reconcile the previously observed 100 document associations, 98 originals, 18,983 active chunks, schema 6, and small-model default with actual current state. Identify the live runtime separately from the archived pilot. Preserve existing user edits.

Implement a pinned PostgreSQL plus pgvector setup suitable for the Windows host, with reproducible startup, extension initialization, schema migrations, and nonsecret configuration examples. Use a maintained PostgreSQL driver, parameterized queries, and registered vector adaptation. Verify the installed extension's storage and index limits: native large-model output is 3,072 dimensions; standard vector HNSW/IVFFlat indexing currently supports up to 2,000. Do not confuse index limits with storage limits.

Migrate the complete application persistence path: documents, sources, extraction revisions, elements, chunks, requirement inventories, fidelity/review records, indexes, activation/configuration records, requests, attempts, adjustments, budget settings, corrections, gold/review records, and evaluation estimates. Inventory every actual table and direct SQL caller. PostgreSQL becomes the authoritative application database; do not leave an independently spendable SQLite ledger active.

Translate SQLite-specific placeholders, PRAGMAs, transactions, conflict handling, row access, schema versioning, JSON, timestamps, and ordering assumptions deliberately. Preserve identifiers, evidence text and offsets, hashes, null/zero distinctions, constraints, and historical records. Keep monetary amounts exact using integer micro-units or an equivalent exact type. Preserve original serialized JSON where byte identity or hashes depend on it; use JSONB only where normalization is safe.

Create and close the bounded PostgreSQL connection pool within the application's resource lifecycle. Define creation, sharing, ownership, checkout timeouts, failure handling, and shutdown. Each operation owns its transaction; executor threads do not share a mutable transaction. Release transactions/connections before provider inference. Close CLI resources on exit. A PostgreSQL failure must never silently redirect writes to SQLite.

Replace BEGIN IMMEDIATE budget admission with PostgreSQL transactions that serialize allowance checks and reservations using row locks or an equivalent proven mechanism. Preserve request idempotency, exactly-once settlement, immutable audit history, unknown-billing recovery, and disabled SDK retries. Enforce one paid-gateway owner across all processes/hosts sharing the database, with explicit lock lifetime and loss behavior. Test independent connections at the spending cap, duplicate dispatch, duplicate settlement, restart, and ownership loss.

Implement a migration CLI with read-only planning/dry-run, consistent source snapshot identity, dependency-ordered bounded imports, resumable checkpoints, and validation. Capture SQLite committed WAL contents through a consistent backup. Rehearse against an isolated paid-disabled PostgreSQL target. Reject unrelated populated targets and changed source snapshots on resume. Repeating an import must neither duplicate records nor overwrite newer target state. Data migration makes no provider calls.

Validate every imported table using row counts and canonical per-record values/digests, including referential integrity, uniqueness, Unicode, balances, pending/unknown attempts, review states, active pointers, and historical citation access. Originals and immutable extraction artifacts may remain in managed files; preserve references and verify hashes/accessibility. Keep private datasets, gold, runtime databases, connection credentials, and source payloads outside Git.

Use pgvector as the selected serving vector store. Store vectors with model, actual dimensions, normalized payload hash, normalization/transformation policy, vector checksum, source index identity, embedding-set version, completeness state, and construction provenance. Deduplicate identical payloads without losing association-specific document/version scope. Preserve historical NumPy artifacts and caches for comparison and rollback; do not silently use them when PostgreSQL is selected.

Change the configured embedding model, relevant defaults, allowlists, supported-dimension checks, estimates, SDK dispatch, service snapshots, evaluation settings, and documentation to text-embedding-3-large. Preserve historical small-model runs and attempts under their original model/rate identities. Inspect database-stored configuration and activated-run overrides so an old record cannot silently keep the new path on small.

Build a genuinely new large-model embedding set from the exact unique chunk payloads. Existing text-embedding-3-small corpus/query vectors are not cache hits for text-embedding-3-large and cannot be converted by truncation, padding, normalization, or relabeling. Reuse only verified large-model entries with matching payload and policy. Re-embed missing corpus payloads and evaluation queries through the existing gateway; populate interactive query caches under the new model identity. The owner authorized paid corpus construction before development labels are frozen; this does not authorize quality acceptance or activation before the required gates.

Use the owner-selected 1,536 dimensions for new text-embedding-3-large corpus and query embeddings, explicitly passing dimensions to the provider. The later owner instruction supersedes the 768-first ladder and smallest-passing selection. Stay below the verified standard vector index limit; do not silently change the selected model or dimensions. Quality acceptance against the native 3,072-dimensional reference remains required before activation.

Use native 3,072-dimensional large-model embeddings as the dimensionality quality reference on a bounded, representative development population. They can be evaluated with exact NumPy or unindexed exact pgvector search; do not attempt a standard vector ANN index on them. Where verified full large-model vectors exist, derive candidate prefixes and L2-renormalize them using the official supported shortening method, preserving original vectors and transformation provenance. Validate derived versus API-shortened behavior on a small paired sample before mixing production methods. Do not regenerate the same inputs separately for every dimension merely to fill an experiment matrix.

Ensure corpus vectors, query vectors, typed database columns, cache keys, settings, estimates, run manifests, activation records, and callers agree on model, dimensions, and transformation policy. Keep dimension variants in separately identified homogeneous sets. Reject mixed-model/dimension searches before provider dispatch or ranking. Check finite nonzero values, expected dimensions, unit normalization, checksums, and row-to-chunk mappings. Preserve historical identities instead of relabeling old caches or results.

Register verified current text-embedding-3-large rates with a new rate version and timestamp before paid execution. Preserve historical attempt price snapshots. Recompute estimates from final unique payload tokens, genuine large-model cache hits, comparison-query misses, and batch limits. Apply the owner-approved $10 allowance and operating cap, expose an exact editable shared limit in Settings, and preserve settled spending, unknown reservations, purpose envelopes and immutable audit history when changing limits. Required owner rate/envelope approvals remain completion conditions; obtain them before paid work. Fewer dimensions reduce storage and arithmetic, not token-priced embedding charges.

Reserve and settle every bounded embedding batch through the gateway. Resume verified completed batches without recharging them; do not resend unknown billed outcomes. Publish only a complete verified candidate set. Handle missing model access or insufficient envelope explicitly and keep the task unfinished until required access/funding decisions are resolved; do not substitute another model or silently omit corpus coverage.

Separate storage, model, dimensionality, and ANN changes in evaluation. First demonstrate NumPy versus pgvector exact-search parity using identical available old-model vectors. Then compare old-model and large-model retrieval on identical source spans, scopes, and chunk policies. Compare large-model reduced candidates against the 3,072-dimensional reference separately. Hold Kiwi BM25, exact requirement lookup, RRF, evidence limits, prompt, generation model, and reranker policy constant. Describe model improvement only when measured.

Keep exact pgvector cosine retrieval as the initial serving implementation, with scope/source-version filters applied to the eligible population and ordinary indexes supporting these predicates. Preserve exact-code handling, deterministic tie order, BM25/RRF ranks, evidence provenance, and visible keyword fallback. Evaluate HNSW separately for broad and narrowly scoped queries, verifying actual query plans, filtered result counts, iterative-scan settings, and recall. Do not select global approximate neighbors and then silently discard needed in-scope evidence.

Freeze an independently reviewed development population before quality evaluation and activation of the owner-selected 1,536-dimensional candidate. Require its nDCG@5 to fall by no more than 0.02 absolute and packed complete-support rate by no more than two percentage points versus the same-model 3,072-dimensional reference, with zero new wrong-scope, exact-code, or critical qualifier/condition failures. Require no new critical failures versus the current lexical/hybrid baseline as well. Report dense-only and hybrid outcomes separately with eligible denominators. If the selected 1,536-dimensional candidate fails, retain safe baseline serving and report the requested reduced-large migration as incomplete; do not weaken acceptance or silently switch models/dimensions.

Benchmark identical-vector NumPy exact, pgvector exact, and optional HNSW retrieval at the chosen dimensions. Record retrieval p50/p95 milliseconds with one and six concurrent clients, warm/cold conditions, ANN neighbor recall@20 against exact search, required-source coverage, vector/table/index storage, construction duration, provider tokens/cost, and authorized end-to-end latency. Use representative EXPLAIN ANALYZE results. Prefer exact search unless HNSW materially improves latency with at least 0.99 mean neighbor recall@20 and no new critical support failure. Exact-search ranking parity permits documented floating-point tolerance and deterministic ties.

Adapt initialization, PostgreSQL backup/restore, index rollback, release reporting, and recovery. Restore the database and referenced immutable artifacts into an isolated paid-disabled runtime and demonstrate historical evidence access. Preserve sealed labels, first sealed results, original model/configuration, and failures unchanged. Do not select model/dimensions by tuning against exposed sealed questions.

After rehearsal and candidate acceptance, cut over in a maintenance window: stop application and maintenance writes, drain dispatched work, preserve unknown billing states, take/validate a final consistent snapshot, import/verify it, then switch PostgreSQL configuration and the large-model embedding set together. Keep SQLite read-only and ensure only PostgreSQL admits paid work. Validate local search, single-document answers, two-document comparisons, verifier traces, review/correction writes, budget status, and original evidence opening. Required owner/local actions remain inside completion.

Provide tested rollback before and after new PostgreSQL writes. Before new writes, revert to the consistent old snapshot and original retrieval configuration. After writes/spending, stop/drain work and reconcile/export all subsequent mutable records and ledger changes into a validated rollback target, or restore a consistent PostgreSQL backup. Never resume stale SQLite spending or operate two writable ledgers. Preserve old-model caches/settings for rollback and leave large-model history intact.

Add focused real-PostgreSQL integration checks for import parity, resume/repeat behavior, transaction contention, pool lifecycle, gateway ownership, small/large cache separation, dimensions dispatch, normalization, mixed-model/dimension rejection, exact ranking parity, filtered ANN, citation identity, and recovery. Use targeted checks during repairs and finish the repository's required independent review process. Mocks do not establish local database/provider acceptance; obtain required local execution before reporting done.

Write the English handover at handoff/postgresql-pgvector/README.md and update setup, runbook, and applicable contracts. Include exact implemented commands for planning, import, validation, embedding estimation/build, dimensionality comparison, activation, cutover, backup, restore, and rollback. Record selected model/dimensions, pinned versions, source/target identities, rate version, costs, performance, checks, private prerequisites, and unresolved limitations. Use UTF-8 without BOM. Finish with a pull request and independent review through the established workflow.
